Reading and editing the Scrapyard code

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
The frame loopFind the code for a changeCode styleFormat the codeCheck a change

Start with the visual contributor guide for the architecture, a hands-on reading path and an end-to-end feature trace.

The frame loop#

Start at scripts/scrapyard.odin. It declares the Godot script's state and its ready/process/exit callbacks. The process callback shows the frame's order:

Odin
typing := poll_frame_ui(self)
// Return here until the script and a session/room are ready.
poll_frame_services(self, typing)
control := sample_gameplay_input(self, typing)
if !advance_gameplay_session(self, dt, control) {
    return
}
update_prediction_smoothing(self)
dispatch_session_changes(self)
present_session_frame(self, dt)

The deferred finish_frame runs when the process callback exits. It runs audio, recording, diagnostics, social/recovery, screen and feedback hooks even when a frame returns early. Their order is intentional. Input edges are captured before session advancement; corrections and event changes are consumed before presentation.

Find the code for a change#

Responsibility File
Input bindings and scene-component setup scripts/scene_setup.odin
Network options, identity/resume, initial world and training encounters scripts/session_start.odin
Profile declaration and lobby actions scripts/lobby_actions.odin
Held controls, overlay guards, discrete actions and development-driver overrides scripts/input.odin
Session advancement, correction smoothing and frame completion scripts/frame.odin
Event fan-out, action outcomes and diagnostic traces scripts/session_events.odin
Observation interpolation and scene presentation scripts/drawing.odin
Gameplay status and local save/status messages scripts/status_view.odin
Development control methods and test/diagnostic queries scripts/development_controls.odin, scripts/probes.odin
Simulation tick, roster changes and player motion shared/game/game.odin
Cast admission/cooldowns and individual ability effects shared/game/abilities.odin, shared/game/ability_casts.odin
Enemy target selection and concrete AI routines shared/game/brains.odin
Workbench admission, encounter setup, confirmation and updates scripts/workbench.odin
Lobby sections, roster, button states and selected loadout scripts/muster.odin
Flame reconciliation/collision and arc presentation scripts/cast_path_view.odin

Files under scripts/ share one Odin package. Helpers receive the values or borrowed world references they need. The script owns the session and Godot handles; the simulation owns gameplay values. Simulation rules remain under shared/game, detached display values under shared/presentation, and authored node behavior under scripts/views. The editor-first guide explains that boundary.

Ability_Cast holds the resolved inputs for one cast; Mob_Pursuit holds one enemy's selected target, distance and speed. They are temporary inputs to ordinary functions. Persistent gameplay values belong in World. Ability handlers share the rule that a killing hit cannot also apply a status to that target.

Code style#

Use multiline procedure bodies and control-flow blocks, one statement per line, and a blank line between meaningful phases. Keep short literals compact. Extract a helper when it names a responsibility, isolates a lifecycle concern, or removes nesting; a flat data table need not become many tiny functions.

Format the code#

The project-local odinfmt.json uses tabs and a 120-column target. From the repository root:

Shell
nix develop --command python3 examples/replay_scrapyard/tools/format.py
nix develop --command python3 examples/replay_scrapyard/tools/format.py --check

The command covers handwritten Odin in scripts, shared code and tools, excluding generated bindings and frozen revision definitions. Godot's format-on-save uses the same configuration. The formatter preserves inline blocks, so write new control flow across lines explicitly.

Formatting a definition extractor or catalog source changes its provenance hash. Rebuild, then use tools/stock.py --project /absolute/path/to/built/project to refresh the artifact receipt. Formatting alone must preserve the canonical catalog digest, schema and semantic content version; it does not justify a new save revision.

Check a change#

Run the model tests when changing gameplay rules:

Shell
nix develop --command odin test tests/replay_scrapyard \
  -collection:godot=. -out:/tmp/replay-scrapyard-model-tests

Use the feature's focused test or workbench when changing an input handler, view, or authored Resource. Changes to an action or saved state also need correction and checkpoint-continuation coverage. The contributor guide lists the model, Godot, and multiplayer checks and explains when each applies.
